title: Engrave and Trace on a whole-model source are never judged: a cut 3-7 mm under the model posts when the stock is turned

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happens:** Engrave and Trace fall to `DepthLaw::None` in `depth_law_of` (crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs) for every source ("they enter the part by design"). Found while auditing the 2D kinds for #1593 (upstream main 7bfb1824 + the #1593 fix).

Probe: the #1585 review fixture (40 x 40 x 8 block, R15 round pocket to Z4, EM-0600-4FL), seeded Engrave / Trace, source `Entity("part")`, top Z8, bottom Z1:
- Both follow every model edge - the R15 pocket ring and the block outline - down to Z1: 516 moves below Z3.9, at radius 15.00..28.28. That is 3 mm under the pocket floor and 7 mm down the outside wall.
- **Stock aligned:** op findings 0; the post is blocked only by the program sim ("gouge: program cuts below the model in 1771 cell(s), worst 7.00 mm at (-19.94, -19.94, z 1.00)").
- **Stock turned 90 deg about Z** (same footprint; the program sim refuses to judge it): op findings 0, and **the post goes out**. `uncovered()` (posting_sim.rs) counts any fresh, stamped op as judged whatever its depth law.

One of the two verdicts is wrong: either this program is a gouge (then it posts on a turned stock - P1), or an engraving on a whole model is always refused on an aligned stock (a false refusal). Read safe side, P1.

**Expected:** an Engrave or Trace on the finished part has a depth law the op itself carries, so the verdict does not depend on whether the program sim can model the stock: a cut deeper than the engraving/trace contract allows is a named gouge on the op and holds the post; a legal engraving posts on both stocks.

**Not the #1593 law:** the Trochoidal slot took `authored_law` (Section) because its geometry is typed. Engrave/Trace cut the part on purpose, so `Section` would convict every legal engraving; this needs its own law (e.g. a depth budget below the traced edge, or refuse on a model source when the program sim cannot judge). Also decide whether `uncovered()` should refuse an op with law `None` on a model source when the sim refuses to judge.

**Done means:** the two repros above give the same verdict with the stock aligned and turned (refused on the op by name for the deep cut), a legal shallow engraving posts on both, pinned through generate and the post, mutation-checked.

Related: #1593, #1550, #1585, #1053.
